purpose: Sarecycline is a prescription antibiotic used to treat moderate to severe acne in people 9 years and older. It helps clear up inflammatory acne breakouts, such as red, swollen pimples and bumps. It is not used for blackheads or whiteheads.
how_it_works: Sarecycline works by stopping the growth of the bacteria that contribute to acne breakouts on your skin. It blocks the bacteria from making the proteins they need to survive and multiply. This helps reduce redness, swelling, and the number of pimples over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, sunburn more easily than usual (sun sensitivity), and vaginal yeast infections in women. You may also notice some stomach upset. Most side effects are mild and tend to get better as your body adjusts.
warnings: Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen daily, as this medication makes your skin much more sensitive to sunburn. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Do not give to children under 9 years old, as it can permanently stain developing teeth. Take with a full glass of water and do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking it to avoid irritating your esophagus.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once daily, with or without food. Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your weight. Try to take it at the same time each day and finish the full course even if your skin starts to improve early.
